summary: The study investigates the wear behavior of quaternary metal oxide coatings, specifically Zn(Ti,Zr)O3, deposited via atomic layer deposition (ALD). The coatings are compared to ternary ZnTiO3 coatings. The quaternary coatings exhibit an amorphous matrix with some nanocrystalline grains, while the ternary coatings show textured (104) nanocolumnar grains. High frequency reciprocating sliding tests reveal that the wear rate is influenced by the crystal structure, with the quaternary coatings showing wear reduction due to a tribofilm and mechanically mixed layer composed of amorphous silica and refined nanocrystalline grains from the coating. The study highlights the role of the fourth element (Zr) in determining the crystalline state and defect structure, which affects tribological properties.
